main_text.l: Indulgeq; cibos (que bonitas tua est) Queis nutrita satis cirpora sentiant Vires nostra nouas legibus & tuis Præscriptum peragant opus. Das maiora, sacris lignaq; laudibus Quum luce irradias pectus Olympica Nostrum vt te metuat teque suum vocet Cunctis temporibus Patrem. Hoc concede bonus te fugientium Spes rerum facili nos capiat dolo, Sed mens nostra tuis, nutibus obsequens Cœlo viuere gaudeat.
carmen Εὐχαριστικὸν propter gemel- las quas vxor Calendis Iunij fauente illius Numine peperit.
SALVE festa dies mihi, Qua coniunx geminas fœta puellulas Partu lætifico valet, Se sperans geminis posse papillulis (Si præstet columem Deus) Mox lactis niuei fundere copiam, Et nutrire gemellulas.

page.notes: The Greek word in the title ("Εὐχαριστικὸν", printed with a long-s-like form) is transcribed from the scan with uncertainty about its exact letters; the ornament rule is not text. The first line of the poem's initial "S" is a woodcut initial, joined to "ALVE". Verse lines are printed in italic and are transcribed as italic-looking script; some letters (e.g. "fugientium", "gaudeat") are slightly blurred. Possible misreadings: "Indulgeq;" and "lignaq;" may be intended as "-que" abbreviations; "columem" likely printed for "columen" but kept as read.
